latest.summary: Online and blended courses can widen opportunities for participation in library and information science education, but delivery mode alone does not explain what students learn. items.title: OFD1 is critical for spermiogenesis by modulating KATNAL2-mediated cytoskeletal remodeling.
items.summary: Cytoskeletal dynamics drive the structural and functional transformation of round spermatids into mature spermatozoa during spermiogenesis. The manchette is a transient microtubule structure in elongating spermatids, while Katanin family proteins regulate its dynamics by severing microtubules to ensure proper germ cell differentiation. However, how Katanin-mediated microtubule remodeling is regulated remains elusive. Here, we identify OFD1, a centrosome-localized ciliopathy-associated protein, as a key regulator of Katanins. OFD1 is highly expressed in the testis, where it dynamically localizes to the acrosome, manchette, and centrosome-structures associated with cytoskeletal networks.…

items.title: Wavelength-Switchable Bidirectional Photoelectric Plasticity in In2Se3 Nanoparticle-Modified In2O3 Nanowires for Neuromorphic Vision.
items.summary: Neuromorphic vision systems require dynamic and multispectral visual processing capabilities to operate in complex environments. However, most optoelectronic synapses still exhibit either a fixed-polarity photoresponse or weak wavelength selectivity, which limits their potential for advanced neuromorphic vision. Here, we report a wavelength-dependent bidirectional optoelectronic synapse based on In2Se3 nanoparticle-modified In2O3 nanowires. We introduce In2Se3 nanoparticles, which are prepared through a facile and scalable liquid-phase exfoliation method, and first employ them to modulate the photoresponse in synaptic devices. The resulting heterostructure broadens the UV spectral response…

items.title: Novel nanoporous-Si-based memristor devices toward neuromorphic computing applications.
items.summary: Porous silicon (PSi), a versatile material with tunable nanoporosity, exhibits a markedly higher surface-to-volume ratio than conventional crystalline silicon (cSi), making it exceptionally attractive for surface-mediated physicochemical processes. Although cSi remains the cornerstone of mainstream microelectronics, the interplay among porosity, carrier dynamics, and interface chemistry in PSi can be harnessed to achieve tunable, high-performance memristive functionality to advance its synaptic behavior. Leveraging these attributes, we design and experimentally validate a reliable memristor structure based on PSi material. We implement the design on an n-type Si wafer using a stack…

items.title: Self-Rectifying ZnO/PZT Ferroelectric Synapses With Polarization-Modulated Transport for Read-Penalty-Resilient Neuromorphic Computing.
items.summary: Sneak-path currents and readout penalties remain critical bottlenecks that limit the scalability and reliability of crossbar-array-based neuromorphic hardware. Here, we experimentally demonstrate self-rectifying Al/ZnO/Pb(Zr 1-x ,Ti x )O 3 ​(PZT)/Pt ferroelectric synapses with polarization-modulated transport and improved weight-update linearity and further evaluate their potential for read-penalty-aware neuromorphic computing through device-informed simulations. The ZnO/PZT heterostructure incorporates a ZnO transport layer that suppresses leakage during polarization switching in PZT while inducing pronounced self-rectifying and nonlinear current-voltage characteristics governed by…

items.title: Biophotonic signaling in living organisms: from electromagnetic communication to physiology, morphogenesis, and morphostasis
items.summary: The aim was to summarize and expand the existing understanding of the communicative role of biophotons in morphogenesis and morphostasis within a working concept of biophoton signaling. The study’s results substantiate the existence of a morphogenetic field and the key role of electromagnetic processes in morphogenesis, morphostasis, and cellular communication. The conclusions characterize the morphogenetic field as a field structure. This review has transdisciplinary significance and informs further development of biophotonics and polaritonics in living organisms.

items.title: A Unified Geometric Space for Topological Alignment Between Transformer-Based Models and Human Brain Networks.
items.summary: Whether artificial neural networks organize information comparably to the human brain remains unclear. Prior brain-AI alignment studies are constrained by specific inputs and tasks, limiting cross-modal comparison. Here we introduce a brain-model topological alignment space that requires no shared task, stimulus, or input dataset. Representing attention heads and seven human intrinsic connectivity networks (ICNs) as graphs, we characterize each with five graph-theoretic metrics and compare their profiles by cosine similarity, yielding a seven-dimensional brain-referenced representation for each head to support dimensionality reduction and model comparison. Across 151 Transformer-based…
items.venue: IEEE transactions on pattern analysis and machine intelligence

items.title: Compactness-aware proposal refinement for foundation model-assisted maize instance annotation in complex field environments
Ten Years of Reinforcement Learning (2016–2026)
items.summary: Between 2016 and 2026, reinforcement learning (RL) expanded from perfect-information board games to large-scale simulation, offline control, language-model post-training, and interactive reasoning agents. Across these settings, much of the algorithmic terminology persisted, including Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS), value estimation, clipped policy ratios, offline conservatism, and self-play. Yet the operating assumptions underneath those methods changed completely with respect to simulator fidelity, logged-data coverage, evaluator reliability, and prior competence. Consequently, classical deep-RL research and modern foundation-model post-training often talk past one another, treating…

items.title: Anatomical deformation modes: a compact scalar-mode subspace for patient-specific deformation modeling.
items.summary: Objective To develop a patient-specific motion-modeling framework that represents a dense three-dimensional deformation vector field (DVF) as a linear combination of scalar-field bases, termed anatomical deformation modes (ADM), with vector coefficients. Approach We formulated ADM as a low-dimensional parameterization of the DVF and showed that it generalizes the vector mode (VM) representation at matched spatial-map storage and provides pose invariance. Patient-specific ADM can be either extracted by principal component analysis (PCA) of the component fields of multiple DVFs or predicted from a single CT image by a deep neural network as a population-learned, anatomy-conditioned prior.…

items.title: Tunable diffusive memristor arrays for neuromorphic temporal computing.
items.summary: The dynamic behaviour of diffusive memristors enables bio-realistic emulation of artificial neurons and synapses, yet scaling from individual devices to neuromorphic systems remains challenging. Stochasticity in ionic motion and filament evolution limits both the uniformity and tunability of these devices, hindering reliable system-level implementation. Here we present a framework for tailoring the relaxation dynamics of diffusive memristors via intrinsic and extrinsic tuning. Percolation in a thin platinum interfacial layer and grain boundaries in a polycrystalline hafnium oxide matrix spatially confine active metal-ion migration; this guided transport substantially improves device…

items.title: Cell-Size-Engineered Ferroelectric Memristors for Wide Reservoir Computing.
items.summary: Hafnium-based ferroelectric memristors are promising for neuromorphic hardware because of their analog switching, low-power operation, and compatibility with complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) technology. Here, cell-size engineering is used to tailor temporal dynamics in ferroelectric memristors with lateral dimensions from 10 × 10 µm 2 to 70 × 70 µm 2 . Smaller cells exhibit slower relaxation and more persistent residual states, whereas larger cells show faster relaxation and shorter-lived responses. These distinct dynamics are interpreted within a domain-statistical framework coupled with depolarization-field-driven polarization relaxation. Measured four-bit pulse responses…

items.title: A gene informed benchmark for BioScoring of pathology foundation models
items.summary: Pathology foundation models are usually compared by their performance on downstream tasks such as classification and retrieval. While such benchmarks measure how useful a model is, they provide no insight into the biology it represents. We introduce BioScore, a benchmark that quantifies how well an image encoder captures cell identities, with spatial transcriptomics of the same tissue as the reference. A sparse autoencoder splits the encoder's patch embeddings into sparse features, which we cluster into a fixed number of groups. BioScore then measures, for each of 52 cell identities defined by marker genes, how specifically one group follows the identity's expression over the tissue.…

items.title: Enhancing Maritime Domain Awareness using Latent Space Representations
items.summary: This work presents a novel application of Earth Observation (EO) embeddings for Maritime Domain Awareness (MDA) from the perspective of the geospatial foundation model TerraMind. By operating directly on compressed latent-space representations rather than on the original Sentinel-1 imagery, this approach directly addresses the data gravity bottleneck that increasingly constrains operational EO processing, in line with the objectives of the Embed2Scale project. In particular, linear and non-linear probing of compressed embeddings, latent space representations of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery, is used to detect, localise, and characterise vessels from Sentinel-1 GRD images. Vessel…

items.title: When to Trust a PFN: Detecting Harmful Shift in Tabular Foundation Models
items.summary: Tabular prior-fitted networks (PFNs) work well across tabular classification problems but can fail silently at deployment when distributions shift. We propose CALD (Calibrated Anchor-Loss Disagreement), a lightweight unsupervised monitor that triggers an alarm to warn when a PFN might fail. By finetuning the decoder to maximize disagreement with the test-set prediction while maintaining accuracy on an ID anchor set, CALD identifies harmful OOD batches through the resulting anchor loss, requiring no labels on test batches. We prove that the post-finetune anchor loss has a strictly lower expectation under sufficiently severe shift than under ID eval, yielding a one-sided test. Across 14…

items.title: Reading, Not Adapting: Unlocking Frozen Visual Knowledge for AI-Generated Image Detection
items.summary: Generalization to unseen image generators has driven efforts to adapt pretrained visual representations for detection. Yet recent findings show that vision foundation models already encode transferable detection knowledge, while further adaptation can impair generalization. This motivates a shift from backbone adaptation to knowledge readout. Conventional linear probing offers a direct way to read this knowledge but is limited to final-layer RGB features. Multi-cue detectors broaden the evidence base, but their designs introduce other tradeoffs: adaptation may compromise pretrained transferability, heterogeneous encoders complicate feature integration, and late fusion precludes…

items.title: Entanglement and HBAR entropy in a Lorentzian non-commutative black hole
items.summary: We investigate how Lorentzian non-commutative smearing affects entanglement and horizon brightened acceleration radiation (HBAR) outside a black hole. For a massless scalar field, tracing over the interior partner gives the exterior quantum channel, its logarithmic negativity, mutual information, and Bell entanglement fidelity. At fixed mass and Killing frequency, increasing the smearing lowers the surface gravity, increases the accessible correlations, and suppresses the leading atomic emission probability. The horizon displacement begins at order $\sqrtΘ$, while the thermal correction at infinity begins at order $Θ$. At fixed local frequency, the redshift introduces a term of order…

items.title: The all-loop spectrum of GGK strings
items.summary: We study the non-perturbative spectrum of the non-relativistic limit of string theory in AdS$_5\times$S$^5$, also known as GGK theory. In light-cone gauge, we show that the bosonic spectrum on a number of vacua is described at all-loops by free massive and massless scalar fields in AdS$_2$, confirming a conjecture by de Leeuw, Fontanella and Nieto-García, arXiv:2403.09563. In static gauge, we obtain the same result for any classical string vacuum, and including fermions. We compute the quantum correction to the classical energy, and show that it vanishes once we adopt the regularised Hurwitz series. We conclude that the quantum energy spectrum built upon any GGK string consists solely of…

items.title: DuCo: Exploiting Dual Cross-Layer Consistency for Sparse Geometric Attention
items.summary: Dense global attention is crucial for capturing cross-view geometry in visual geometry foundation models, yet its quadratic complexity limits efficient inference on long image sequences. Existing sparse attention methods primarily select entries of the global attention matrix based on attention probabilities and construct masks independently across layers, overlooking value redundancy and cross-layer information reuse. By analyzing attention distributions and clustering value representations across layers, we reveal two forms of \emph{cross-layer consistency}, characterized by highly similar attention probability distributions and localized changes in value redundancy structures. Building…

items.title: Gravitational collapse to extremal black holes with $Λ>0$: counterexamples to the third law without charge
items.summary: We study the dynamical formation of the extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter solution, in both its time orientations, and the related Nariai solution. We prove that there exist spherically symmetric, regular Cauchy data for the Einstein-scalar field system with $\mathbb S^3$ topology, for any scalar field mass $\mathfrak{m}\geq 0$, that lead to the formation of an exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole in finite time, and that moreover the apparent horizon of the solution is exactly isometric to that of the subextremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter solution at earlier times. We also show that if the scalar field mass satisfies $\mathfrak{m}>\sqrtΛ/2$, an analogous result holds having…

items.title: Rank Before You Encode: Reading a Few Percent of a Whole-Slide Image
items.summary: Classifying a whole-slide image requires encoding thousands of high-resolution tiles with a pathology foundation model, which accounts for most of the inference cost. Existing efficient methods reduce this cost by selecting fewer tiles, but typically train a new model around their selection strategy. A largely unexplored alternative is to keep an existing full-bag model frozen and run it on selected tiles at the same encoder cost. We introduce this comparison, alongside random tile sampling at matched cost. To select tiles, we fit a lightweight selector with 3.3K parameters to the attention of a frozen model, without additional slide labels. The selector ranks regions from a slide…

items.title: A Genetic Algorithm Approach to Reconstructing Scalar-Tensor Lagrangians
items.summary: Recent DESI baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) data, combined with cosmic microwave background (CMB) and Type Ia supernovae observations, have been interpreted as evidence for dynamical dark energy whose equation of state crosses the phantom divide $w=-1$. Such a crossing cannot be realized smoothly by a minimally coupled scalar field $\varphi$, but can arise naturally in scalar-tensor theories. We present a data-driven framework that reconstructs the scalar-tensor Lagrangian directly from observations, using a genetic algorithm to evolve the symbolic expressions for the nonminimal coupling $F(\varphi)$ and the scalar potential $U(\varphi)$. Each candidate is evaluated through a forward…

items.title: Inverted Pendulum in the Sky: Floquet Stabilization of Cosmological Axions
items.summary: Many cosmological scenarios require a scalar field to sit near the top of its potential, which usually requires a fine-tuned initial condition. We ask whether the hilltop of an axion potential can be dynamically stabilized by a rapidly oscillating coupling, as for the inverted pendulum of Kapitza, and to what extent this can reduce the fine-tuning. Using Floquet theory, we determine the stability window of the hilltop and analyze several realizations: an oscillating coupling, a spinning or oscillating second field, and a gyroscopic analogue, an inverted spinning top realized by a sigma model on a squashed three-sphere. In an expanding Universe the stabilized phase lasts for a number of…

items.title: Can Visual World Models See Force?
items.summary: World models and vision-language-action policy models are increasingly proposed as foundations for robot manipulation. They predict how scenes evolve and which actions to take, yet successful manipulation depends not solely on following observable trajectories but also on the hidden variable of interaction force. Neurophysiology has shown that humans possess a visual prior for this hidden variable, motivating us to ask the question: Do the representations of visual foundation models also capture the forces involved in an interaction? We define force awareness as the ability of representations to (1) indicate when contact force is applied, (2) track how it changes during an interaction, and…

items.title: Decoupling the clocks of learning and computing in spiking neural networks
items.summary: Biological intelligence thrives on minimal power despite its noisy, imperfect components, with neurons that communicate through voltage spikes. Brain-inspired computing seeks to bring such efficiency to real devices, which requires training methods tailored to them. The standard way to train spiking neural networks, backpropagation through time, computes weight updates through every step of a simulated device, so faithful or long simulations can make training costly and unstable. Here we show that spiking networks can learn reliably and efficiently by decoupling the clock of learning from that of computing. Our method, ChronoProp, calculates weight updates from each neuron's spike counts…

items.title: Robin--Hadamard states for unstable field in half-Minkowski spacetime
items.summary: We investigate the quantization of a real massless scalar field in four-dimensional half-Minkowski spacetime subject to an attractive Robin boundary condition. We show that the unstable modes, required for classical spectral completeness, are also essential to recover the canonical commutation relations (CCR) of the complete quantum field. By specifying the Cauchy covariances of the unstable sector, we construct a family of positive quasifree states compatible with the conservation of total energy. Within this family, positivity is incompatible with stationarity, so that the resulting states necessarily break the time-translation symmetry of the background. We also obtain a closed…

items.title: StateWeaver: Multi-Agent Coordination of Story-State Transitions for Long-Horizon Video Generation
items.summary: Modern video foundation models generate high-quality short clips, but preserving long-video consistency and correctly depicting event-driven state changes remain challenging. Existing agentic workflows face these challenges because continual planning and repair accumulate context, while reference updates remain limited. We introduce StateWeaver, which combines Active States and Hierarchical Collaboration to connect review-driven visual reference updates with cross-shot state inheritance. Active States translate state discrepancies identified during review into concrete visual asset requirements that guide reference construction, validation, and regeneration, preserving identity and…

items.title: Sharp decay and regularity thresholds for Minkowski stability in spherical symmetry
items.summary: We establish sharp decay and regularity thresholds for Minkowski stability in the spherically symmetric Einstein--scalar field system. For small smooth characteristic data measured in weighted derivative seminorms, we prove global stability at borderline decay and half-derivative regularity of the initial data. The resulting developments remain uniformly close to Minkowski spacetime and are future causally geodesically complete. Both thresholds are sharp: below either the decay or regularity threshold, we construct arbitrarily small smooth, initially untrapped data whose developments contain trapped spheres.

items.title: Analemma $\infty$: A Temporal Benchmark for Geospatial Foundation Models
items.summary: Satellite time series capture how land surfaces change over time. Pixel-wise temporal foundation models read a year of satellite observations per pixel, yet public benchmarks lack a temporal axis or subsample it to a few dates. We introduce Analemma, a temporal benchmark of six datasets that carry every 10 and 20 m Sentinel-2 band and a time series spanning a growing season, completed where their releases omit geometry, dates, or cloud masks. One frozen-encoder protocol evaluates all models across label ratios and three seeds, with two baselines without pretraining. The TESSERA model ranks first overall. A from-scratch model on monthly composites outranks every foundation model except…

items.title: On the Fueter--Sce--Qian theorem for partial-slice monogenic functions
items.summary: The notion of partial-slice monogenic functions has recently been introduced to provide a unified framework encompassing both monogenic and slice monogenic functions over Clifford algebras. In this new setting, we establish some fractional Laplacian identities for the Cauchy kernels and their derivatives in the sense of tempered distributions. These identities allow us to prove a termwise Fueter--Sce--Qian theorem for partial-slice monogenic functions represented by convergent Laurent series consisting only of principal parts.

items.title: Text-Conditioned Low-Rank Adaptation of Time-Series Foundation Models for Multimodal Forecasting
items.summary: Time-series foundation models (TSFMs) provide transferable numerical forecasting priors. However, forecast-relevant information may be conveyed in text without being reflected in the observed series. Many multimodal forecasting methods integrate such context through model inputs or intermediate representations. We investigate a complementary mechanism: text-conditioned parameter adaptation. We propose Context-to-LoRA for Time Series (C2LoRA-TS), which encodes text and generates temporary Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) updates for selected weight matrices of a frozen TSFM. Both the numerical backbone and text encoder remain frozen, and the method exactly recovers the frozen TSFM output when…

items.title: Not Every Input Needs Everything: Unifying Expert Gating, Model Cascades, and Agent Orchestration
items.summary: Executing monolithic neural weights, frontier foundation models, or entire multi-agent workflows uniformly on every input incurs substantial computational, latency, and monetary overhead. Conditional computation mitigates this cost by deciding dynamically which internal experts, model endpoints, or specialized agents to invoke per request. Yet token-level gating in sparse neural architectures, query-level model cascades, and task-level multi-agent coordination have largely progressed in disconnected research silos, obscuring recurring system failures and transferable fixes. In this systematic review, we synthesize 2,289 studies published between 2017 and September 2026 (selected from…

items.title: FoMNet: Adaptive Kernels Meet Contextual Matching for Cross-Modal Homography Estimation
items.summary: Cross-modal homography estimation requires reliable correspondences despite appearance differences between sensing modalities. Multi-scale refinement progressively reduces the search range, but its accuracy remains limited by the ability of matching features to distinguish nearby candidates. The vision foundation model (VFM) provides complementary representations, yet integrating these features through fixed interpolation leaves their spatial aggregation independent of image content and the correspondence objective. We propose the Foundation Model-Enhanced Matching Network (FoMNet), which combines learned spatial adaptation of VFM features with contextual correspondence estimation. Patch…

items.title: MoSk: A Unified Motion-Skeleton Foundation Model for Human Motion Understanding and Generation
items.summary: Foundation models (FMs) have advanced visual understanding and generation by providing semantically rich representations. However, this role of FMs remains underexplored in human motion. Large motion datasets offer diverse movements at scale, but often lack action labels for systematically evaluating learned representations on understanding tasks. Skeleton datasets enable such evaluation through established recognition protocols, yet are typically smaller and focus on predefined actions captured in controlled environments. To combine these strengths, we present MoSk, to the best of our knowledge, the first Motion-Skeleton foundation model to integrate motion and skeleton datasets. MoSk…

items.title: Rethinking Unsupervised Cross-Modal Homography Estimation:Spatially Aware Representations and Geometric Consistency Learning
items.summary: Unsupervised cross-modal homography estimation is challenging because appearance differences obscure shared geometric structures. Separating modality transfer from homography estimation helps reduce these differences, but accurate alignment still requires effective geometric representations and consistency constraints on the two subtasks. We propose GeoCo (Geometry-Aware and Consistency-Constrained Homography Estimation), a framework that addresses these two requirements without cross-modal transformation labels. Its homography estimator, RVHomo, adapts hierarchical features from a frozen vision foundation model (VFM) and fuses them with local CNN features to capture structural context and…

items.title: Assessing the Physical Interpretability of AlphaEarth Foundation Embeddings Through Multi-Sensor Satellite Time-Series Benchmarking for Agricultural Mapping
items.summary: Accurate and dynamic maps of agricultural LULC are important for agricultural water resource management, particularly in areas where water scarcity is prevalent, such as Morocco. Here, we evaluate the utility of AlphaEarth Foundation Model (AEF) embeddings for agricultural LULC and irrigation-type mapping in Morocco. AEF embeddings were compared to single-date and time-series remote-sensing features using three machine-learning classifiers: XGBoost, CatBoost, and TabPFN. We also evaluated whether AEF embeddings can: (a) provide an efficient and transferable alternative to conventional direct use of Earth observation products and (b) reconstruct biophysical information. Results showed that…

items.title: geo-eval-harness: An Evaluation Harness for Geospatial Foundation Models
items.summary: Geospatial foundation model (GFM) research papers are plagued by inconsistent evaluation settings (e.g., different pre-processing and probes), making it difficult to separate performance from evaluation choices. We propose geo-eval-harness}, an open-source framework for controlled model comparisons. We use this harness to evaluate 100 GFMs and general vision models on 6 classification and 14 segmentation datasets, using multiple probes on frozen or low-rank-adapted encoders. We show that under controlled evaluation, general vision backbones are competitive on RGB classification and high-resolution segmentation, but GFMs shine on multispectral tasks. When we compare any two of the top-ten…

items.title: Quaternion-Tucker ZigZag Networks: Halving Transformer Backbone Parameters and Enabling Exact 2D Zero-Loss Continual Scaling
items.summary: Standard Transformers allocate independent dense weight matrices to every feed-forward network (FFN) layer, coupling parameters linearly with depth (O(L)) and discarding prior compute when scaling capacity. Conversely, weight-tied Looped Transformers decouple depth from parameters (O(1)) but enforce time-homogeneous updates. We formulate the L-layer FFN stack as a 3D Tensor Cuboid and introduce QuatTucker-ZigZagGPT, unifying: (1) 4D Quaternion Hamilton GEMMs in bfloat16 (4x FFN compression), (2) 64x64 Block-Diagonal Tucker SwiGLU Cores for depth-specific rotations over a shared basis, (3) Braided ZigZag Diamond Routing (L0 -> L2 -> L1 -> L3) for zero-FLOP top-down refinement, and (4) Exact…

items.title: Ferroionic CuCrP2S6 Integrated Silicon Photonics for Neuromorphic Computing
items.summary: Neuromorphic photonic computing calls for optical states that combine stimulus accumulation, spontaneous relaxation, and nonvolatile state retention without continuous power dissipation. Here, we demonstrate a ferroionic photonic platform by integrating layered van der Waals CuCrP2S6 onto silicon microring resonators using a back-end integration process. Electrical pulsing produces unidirectional blue shifts in the optical resonance, consistent with field-driven redistribution of mobile Cu ions and giving rise to a history-dependent optical response. The resulting optical state is strongly pulse dependent, exhibiting both volatile and nonvolatile components. A short 20-pulse excitation…

items.title: Connecting AI Agents to Live Discrete Element Simulations via the Model Context Protocol
items.summary: This paper describes a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server through which a general-purpose AI agent operates a discrete element engine, commercial or open-source, while the simulation runs. The agent submits a long simulation to the engine and, while it computes, reads the running model, changes it, or stops it. The human modeler stays at the engine's console and graphical interface throughout, and the agent sees what the modeler does there. The tools are derived from what the agent needs to do at the engine and are held to four principles: correctness, coverage, orthogonality and simplicity. Two documentation tools let the agent search the engine's manual and browse it level by level.…

items.title: SEEK: Self-Evolution through Execution Knowledge for Agentic Robot Manipulation
items.summary: General-purpose multimodal foundation models enable robots to adapt during deployment from observations and execution feedback, without task-specific demonstrations or training. However, the robot retains what it learns only in the model's working context. Once the task ends, it loses this execution knowledge, such as how to carry a bowl between two grippers. On the next attempt at the task, the robot may take just as long and repeat the same mistakes. To avoid this repetition, robots must retain execution knowledge across attempts. Yet replaying past actions is insufficient, because their effects depend on the current conditions. Procedures that determine actions from the current scene…

items.title: EGSE: Evidence-Grounded Skill Evolution for Medical Reasoning Agents
items.summary: Medical reasoning agents combine foundation models with specialized tools to interpret medical images, yet reusing their historical experience remains challenging. A correct final answer can conceal flawed reasoning or tool use, synthesized advice may lack source support, and superficially similar cases may require different diagnostic procedures. In this paper, we propose EGSE, an evidence-grounded skill evolution framework that distills historical dialogues from similar cases into reusable conditional workflows and progressively refines a multi-faceted skill library through supported and validated updates to improve medical agents. EGSE evaluates intermediate reasoning and tool use and…

items.title: Continuous Foundation-Guided Pseudo-Label Weighting for Breast Ultrasound Domain Adaptation
items.summary: Breast ultrasound segmentation models often generalize poorly across scanners, institutions, and patient populations. We investigate continuous foundation-guided pseudo-label weighting for unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA). An exponential-moving-average (EMA) teacher generates target-domain pseudo-labels, while a frozen ultrasound segmentation model (AutoSAMUS) modulates their contribution using a bounded weight that combines the prior's certainty with its probabilistic agreement with the teacher. In contrast to our earlier selective BiRP rule, the proposed formulation supervises every target pixel with a weight in [0.5, 1] and requires no foundation-model inference at test time. We…

items.title: Bridging Transferability and Discriminability via Positive-Unlabeled Domain Adaptation for Building Damage Mapping Across Disaster Events
items.summary: Mapping the damage to buildings following natural and human-caused disasters is essential for disaster response and humanitarian assistance. However, differences in hazard types, geographic environments, building characteristics, and imaging conditions cause cross-event distribution shifts that limit the generalization of deep learning models to new disaster events, even for geospatial foundation models (GFMs) pretrained on extensive Earth observation data. Unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) can mitigate these shifts, but adaptation remains challenging when damage-proportion and damage-appearance shifts coexist and interact. We identify enhancing target-domain discriminability as key to…

items.title: Triage Before Fine-Tuning: Feasibility-Gated Selection and Monitored Adaptation of Embodied Foundation Models for a Fixed Physical Platform
items.summary: Embodied foundation models are increasingly deployed by selection: a practitioner picks a public checkpoint by benchmark rank and fine-tunes it on local data. The platform is fixed before the model is chosen, with little or no local data. We ask what such a checkpoint loses on a fixed platform and which part of the loss local data can buy back. We split the gap by what can repair it. A sensing gap, information the sensors do not capture, cannot be closed with their data; a latency gap, output arriving after the control loop needs it, belongs to the loop, not the weights; only a distribution gap is fine-tuning's to repair. TRIAGE turns this into feasibility-gated selection and monitored…

items.title: Mushroom species-specific ergothioneine and phenolic enrichment in solid-state fermented wheat grains as drivers of enhanced antioxidant capacity
items.summary: Abstract Edible and medicinal mushrooms are valued for their bioactive compounds with established health benefits. Mycelium-enriched cereals are an emerging source of mycochemicals with natural antioxidant activity for functional food applications. To assess species-specific potential for antioxidant enrichment and secondary metabolite accumulation, we evaluated eight commercially cultivated fungal species using solid-state fermentation of wheat grains under standardized conditions. We quantified total antioxidant capacity (QUENCHER-CUPRAC), ergothioneine (EGT), total phenolic content (TPC), and flavonoids in myceliated wheat and uninoculated controls (n = 4 per species). All species…

items.title: Closing the Loop on Automated Feature Engineering: A Heart-Failure Pilot
items.summary: Abstract Heart-failure risk models draw on variables scattered across diagnoses, medications, laboratory results and procedures. The features built from these records are made by hand for each dataset, with no record of the evidence behind them. We evaluate the Nimblemind Multi-Agent System (nMAS), whose recursive self-improvement (RSI) loop proposes features and model weights from published knowledge. Each predictor mined from the heart-failure literature is built as a feature and kept only if it improves a fixed model on the hospital's own patients. The loop was applied to a synthetic cohort of 10,000 records, 31,427 MIMIC-IV patients and 26,168 patients of a United States health system,…

items.title: When Models Build Their Own Machines: From Silicon to Self-Scaling Intelligence
items.summary: Every model runs on a machine it did not design. This is changing. Language models write RTL, tune kernels and orchestrate EDA flows. They are beginning to help design the chips that train and serve them. As models improve chips and chips train stronger models, intelligence may scale beyond software alone. We treat the chip as the physical layer of recursive self-improvement, describe the co-evolution of model, software stack and silicon as a dynamical system, and propose the Levels of Self-Scaling Intelligence L0–L6, from design assistance, autonomous optimization and end-to-end design to self-improvement and cross-layer co-evolution, with recursive self-expansion and open-ended…

items.title: Continual learning in oncology AI: A framework for safe clinical translation.
items.summary: AI models remain largely static, yet cancer care never stands still. Evolution of scanning technology, imaging protocols, staging criteria, therapies, and patient populations can silently erode model performance and patient safety. Continual learning (CL) enables models to continuously acquire new knowledge, while minimizing catastrophic forgetting. Here, we review CL methods and their oncology applications, predominantly in imaging and pathology, and discuss CL as an option for maintaining foundation models, alongside recalibration and retraining. We examine translational barriers, including hidden regressions in underrepresented populations, label and concept drift, privacy constraints…

items.title: LoopROS: A Deployable Embodied Recursive Self-Improvement Framework Based on Logical and Physical Constraints
items.summary: Embodied recursive self-improvement (RSI) endows robots with the capacity to progressively refine manipulation skills through real-world physical interaction, representing a cornerstone toward generalpurpose embodied intelligence. Yet existing embodied RSI frameworks largely remain simulationbound: they fail to realize closed-loop RSI when transferred onto uncalibrated real-world robots. This paper presents LoopROS, a deployable RSI framework built upon a constraints-as-policy principle for embodied robot. With In-Context Learning-Based Logical Constraints, the LoopROS parses real-world demonstrations, to guide segment selection, outcome assessment, and experience reuse. With Segmentwise…

items.title: From Recursive Self-Improvement to Human-AI Reciprocal Improvement
items.summary: Recursive self-improvement advances most readily in domains where results can be verified reliably, such as mathematics and coding. Beyond these domains, progress slows as reliable signals for evaluating and guiding improvement become harder to obtain, resulting in a jagged frontier of AI capabilities. Yet even where AI self-improves autonomously, its growing capabilities do not necessarily translate into greater human ability to understand, use and build upon its outputs, challenging both continued human participation and effective oversight. We argue that recursive progress should therefore also encompass the growth of human capabilities. We propose Recursive Reciprocal Improvement (RRI)…

items.title: Hyperbolic neural networks for biologically informed classification of white blood cells and hematopoietic cell states in peripheral blood smears
items.summary: Abstract Automated white blood cell (WBC) classification in peripheral blood smears supports morphological assessment of hematological disorders, but most deep learning classifiers treat cell categories as independent labels and do not account for hematopoietic maturation. We propose a hyperbolic classification framework that combines a ResNet-18 feature extractor with a prototype-based classifier in the Poincaré ball, allowing biologically related cell states to be represented in a geometry suited to hierarchical structure. items.title: NeuroMASS v4: Geometry-Aware Neural Population Dynamics via Learnable Hyperbolic Latent Representations and Biologically-Calibrated Diagonal State Space Models
items.summary: The geometry of neural population activity is a fundamental challenge in computational neuroscience. We present NeuroMASS v4, a novel architecture that introduces learnable hyperbolic latent geometry to spike-train co-smoothing on the Neural Latents Benchmark (NLB’21). Our central scientific claim is that the curvature c of a Poincaré-ball—learned end-to-end from extracellular spike recordings— constitutes a biologically interpretable geometric signature: significantly positive for ring-manifold motor circuits (MC_Maze, MC_RTT) and near-zero for topologically unstructured frontal circuits (DMFC_RSG). items.title: From quantum brain to quantum mind: The ontological promotion gap in quantum-biological theories of consciousness.
items.summary: Quantum effects in biological systems are increasingly investigated at molecular, cellular, and neural scales, yet evidence for quantum organization in a living brain does not by itself determine the ontological status of the conscious states realized by that brain. This article distinguishes seven claims often compressed under "quantum consciousness": quantum occurrence, causal relevance, constitutive relevance, phenomenal bridging, phenomenal individuation, quantum mental status, and quantum-formal adequacy. It argues that evidence for the first three-even if decisive-does not by itself establish quantum mental status. I call this cross-level inferential discontinuity the Ontological…

items.title: BioLM-Score: Language-Prior Conditioned Probabilistic Geometric Potentials for Protein-Ligand Scoring.
items.summary: Motivation Protein-ligand scoring must address affinity prediction, pose selection, and virtual screening, but these objectives are not necessarily optimized together. Geometric likelihood models may generalize poorly when training-set structural coverage is limited. We test whether pretrained biomolecular representations improve scoring under a controlled geometric baseline. Results BioLM-Score integrates frozen protein and molecular language-model embeddings into a residue-atom distance-likelihood framework via gated graph convolutions. We evaluate geometry-only, jointly trained, and two-stage fine-tuned variants, using the jointly trained variant for the primary controlled comparisons.…

items.title: HERACLES for fast and accurate likelihood-based reconstruction of massive lineages
items.summary: CRISPR-based lineage recording technologies can trace the ancestry of hundreds of thousands of cells, yet reconstructing accurate phylogenies at this scale remains computationally challenging. Likelihood-based methods employ explicit evolutionary models of CRISPR editing that improve tree accuracy but require computationally expensive searches over tree topologies, whereas greedy distance-based alternatives scale efficiently but their accuracy requires distances that faithfully represent the true phylogeny. Here, we introduce HERACLES, which optimizes cell coordinates in hyperbolic space under a quartet-based composite likelihood of CRISPR editing. By recovering local branching structures…

items.summary: Background: Hyperbolic embedding of Hi-C matrices into a Poincaré disc recovers the full TAD hierarchy from a single embedding. items.title: How many labels can a biological oscillator carry? A quality-factor screen for proposed information carriers.
items.summary: How many distinguishable labels can a biological oscillator carry? Proposals invoking collective vibrational modes, endogenous electromagnetic fields, microtubule excitations and oscillatory phase codes are each debated on grounds particular to themselves, with no shared standard for comparison. We show that spectral distinguishability alone bounds the number of labels by the quality factor, M≤Q=2πντ coh . It follows from the relation between linewidth and coherence time, is independent of substrate, mechanism and any position on quantum effects in biology, and can be evaluated from two published quantities. Applied to a recently proposed 30 GHz intracolumnar microwave field in cortex, it…

items.title: Hierarchical semantic fusion in hyperbolic space for next POI recommendation.
items.summary: Next Point-of-Interest (POI) recommendation aims to suggest POIs that users are likely to visit next based on their recent check-ins. Recent studies suggest that POI-POI transitions and user-POI interactions exhibit hierarchical patterns that can be modeled in hyperbolic space, whose exponential volume growth enables compact and expressive representations. However, existing hyperbolic methods insufficiently explore rich contextual semantics, such as category and region information, and thus fail to leverage these signals when modeling user mobility patterns. items.title: Unraveling the Ultrafast Photodynamics of Molecular Photoswitches in β-Adrenergic Receptors by First-Principles Nonadiabatic Dynamics Simulations.
items.summary: Understanding how protein environments regulate the photodynamics of chromophores is a central task in quantum biology and remains a major challenge. This challenge is particularly significant for G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), which are natively nonphotochromic but can be optically controlled via synthetic photoswitchable ligands. Such artificial photoreceptors are new and important because they not only enable the photocontrol of signaling processes beyond those regulated by rhodopsins but also deepen our fundamental understanding of quantum effects in light-protein interactions. However, the ultrafast nonadiabatic dynamics of these ligands in GPCRs remain difficult to resolve…
